newsitem.title: USA: Nintendo says new game system sells out in three days.
newsitem.headline: Nintendo says new game system sells out in three days.

text.p: Nintendo Co. Ltd, the maker of video game systems, said Wednesday its entire 350,000-unit shipment of new N64 video game players had sold out at retail stores three days after their launch Sunday.
"There were widespread spot shortages within hours of stores opening Sunday morning," Howard Lincoln, chairman Nintendo of America, said in a statement.

Nintendo of America is the U.S. unit of Kyoto, Japan-based Nintendo. Nintendo 64, known as N64, is Nintendo's widely anticipated 64-bit game player that improves the graphics and speed of its older 16-bit system.
The product's launch heightens the battle for market share in the billion-dollar video game business among N64, Sony Corp.'s Playstation and Sega Enterprises Ltd.'s Saturn game players.
Lincoln said he was optimistic the parent company will send enough players to ensure supplies are adequate over the holidays. N64 has been available in Japan since early summer.

Nintendo had planned to sell 600,000 units in the United States through the holiday season. Lincoln now predicts U.S. retailers can sell over 1.5 million units "if there is any way to receive that much inventory from Japan."
